info.title: Open Alvary API
info.description: Read-only access to the published Open Alvary corpus for organisations with access. Send an API key or access token as `Authorization: Bearer <credential>`.

400.description: A parameter, filter, cursor or token is not valid (`invalid_input`, `invalid_filter`, `unsupported_filter`, `invalid_cursor`).

401.description: No key or token, or one that is unknown, revoked, expired or for another resource (`credential_required`, `invalid_credentials`). WWW-Authenticate says where to get one.

403.description: The organisation has no access, or the record is outside it (`entitlement_required`, `entitlement_lapsed`, `jurisdiction_not_included`, `insufficient_scope`, `account_inactive`, `organisation_suspended`).

409.description: The cursor expired, or the feed was reset (`stale_cursor`, `feed_reset`).

410.description: Changes after this position are no longer kept (`replay_window_expired`).

429.description: An allowance is used up for now (`rate_limited`). Retry-After says when to try again.

503.description: Access or the corpus cannot be checked right now (`temporarily_unavailable`, `capacity_exhausted`). Try again after Retry-After.

get.description: Changes in the order they were made, oldest first: records added, corrected or withdrawn, texts published and coverage changes. Keep the `resume_token` and send it next time for only newer changes. Send at most one of `cursor`, `resume_token` and `start`. The same route answers without a key at https://open.alvary.ai/api/changes.

parameters.name: jurisdiction
parameters.description: Jurisdiction IDs, such as `ng`; a country includes its states and local law. Up to 50.

parameters.name: work
parameters.description: Record IDs, such as `ng-foi-act-2011`. Up to 50.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Kinds of change: `catalogue_added`, `metadata_corrected`, `text_version_published`, `withdrawal`, `coverage_changed`.

parameters.name: class
parameters.description: Document types, such as `act` or `regulation`. Up to 50.

parameters.name: language
parameters.description: Languages of the affected text, such as `en`. Up to 50.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: A keyword: whole words in the title, citation or summary, ignoring case. Up to 200 characters.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Changes per page, 1 to 100. Default 25.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `next_cursor` of the previous page, to continue the same window (15 minutes).

parameters.name: resume_token
parameters.description: The `resume_token` of an earlier answer: changes after it, in a new window.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: `now`: no changes, only a resume token at the latest position.

get.description: The latest changes of the last 90 days, newest first (up to 50), with the same filters. For showing what's new, not for keeping up: use List changes for that.

get.description: Passages of published texts that match the words, best first: each hit is a section, article or schedule paragraph, with a snippet of the exact text, its byte span and the anchor to get it whole. Only published texts are searched; `coverage` says how many records in the scope have one, and `status` tells no result (`no_result`) apart from a scope with no published text (`unsupported_scope`) and a search that could not run (`degraded`). A query that reads as a citation of a part, such as `NDPA s. 23(1)(a)`, puts that part first. Without `jurisdiction`, a search covers your plan's countries.

parameters.description: The citation, such as `Act No. 4 of 2011` or `FOI Act 2011, s. 1(1)`.

parameters.name: as_of
parameters.description: A date, such as `2024-01-01`: look for the part only in texts in force on it.

parameters.name: language

Problem.description: A refusal (RFC 9457). Its `code` is explained at https://open.alvary.ai/docs/errors.

type.description: A link to the code's explanation.

detail.description: What happened and what to do, in a sentence.

retryable.description: Whether the same request may succeed later.

request_id.description: Quote it when you ask us about this request.

retry_after_seconds.description: When to try again, as Retry-After.

ChangeWork.description: The record a change is about.

legal_status.description: Whether it is in force now, as the catalogue has it: `current`, `historical`, `repealed`, `superseded` or `unknown`.

api_url.description: The record in this API: Get a record.

schema_version.description: The version of this shape, `change-event-1`. New event types and fields may appear within a version: ignore the ones you do not know.

event_revision.description: 1, or higher when we corrected the change itself (see `supersedes`).

event_type.description: What changed: `catalogue_added` (a record added: an old law newly catalogued, not a new law), `metadata_corrected` (its catalogue details corrected), `text_version_published`, `legal_effect_recorded` (a checked repeal, amendment or supersession of the record by another public record), `withdrawal` (a record or text) or `coverage_changed` (a jurisdiction's coverage). More types may be added: ignore those you do not know; `/change-coverage` lists the ones recorded.

feed_epoch.description: The feed's epoch; it changes only when the feed is reset.

publication_revision.description: The catalogue's revision it was made in.

observed_at.description: When the change was seen at the official source, if known.

publisher_published_at.description: When the publisher published it, if known.

legal_effective.description: When it takes legal effect, if known.

work.description: The record, or null when it may no longer be named.

version.description: For a published or withdrawn text: {id, content_hash, language}.

rights_revision.description: For a published or withdrawn text: the revision of the record's rights record in force (see `/rights/{source_id}/history`).

changed_fields.description: For a correction: the fields that changed. A correction never changes legal text.

supersedes.description: For a corrected change: the {event_id, event_revision} it replaces.

summary.description: One plain sentence saying what changed.

withdrawal.description: For a withdrawal: {scope_disclosure, action, reason_code}. A text version withdrawn from a record that stays public is `named`, with the version in `version`, `action` `stop_serving` (stop serving copies of that text) and `reason_code` `rights_changed` (its rights record changed or lapsed) or `correction` (its approval was withdrawn). When `scope_disclosure` is `revalidate_releases`, check your copies against a current release.

legal_effect.description: For a legal effect: {kind, by, effective_date, evidence_url}. `kind` is `repeal`, `amendment` or `supersession` of the record in `work`; `by` is the record that had the effect {id, title, citation}; the date is when it took effect, when known. A reviewer checked it against the official text. A later correction of it has the same `event_id`.

previous.description: For a correction: the previous values of the fields that changed, among `legal_status`, `rights_status`, `document_type` and `year`.

version_diff.description: For a text that replaces an earlier one: {prior_version_id, added, removed, changed, truncated}, the locators of the provisions added, removed and changed (their words differ), in document order, at most 200 each.

events.description: This page's changes, oldest first. A page may be short or empty.

has_more.description: Whether to ask again with `next_cursor` now.

next_cursor.description: Send as `cursor` for the next page (within 15 minutes).

resume_token.description: Keep it; send it later for only newer changes.

jurisdictions.description: Per jurisdiction: {id, name, works, readable_works, last_change_at, last_checked_at, expected_cadence, known_gaps}.

allowance.description: Its limits: requests_per_minute, burst, concurrency, bytes_per_day, jurisdictions (countries of your choice, when limited), watches (monitors), digest, shared_watches, webhook_endpoints.

listing.description: How the console shows it: order, for, price, action, note.

download_base.description: Where its files are; append `/` and a file name.

files.description: Its files, with their SHA-256 checksums.

bearer.description: An API key (`oa_live_…`) from the console, or an access token from a connected app.
